correctness.rationale: The coefficient polynomial extends the integer sequence without assuming that the tuple count is defined at arbitrary 5-adic parameters. I checked the logarithmic derivative b_m=σ₁(m)−25·1_{5|m}σ₁(m/5) and the coefficient recurrence. The decisive finite certificate was independently replayed by truncated Euler-product multiplication, not by executing the frozen verifier or reusing its recurrence: set K=111+125X, start with 1, and for m=1,...,39 multiply by sum_{0≤j≤floor(39/m)} (−1)^j binom(M,j) q^{mj}, with M=4K if 5|m and M=−K otherwise; discard q-powers above 39 at each step. Use binom(M,0)=1 and binom(M,j+1)=binom(M,j)(M−j)/(j+1) in exact rational polynomials. The replay found v₅(c₀)=5, v₅(c₁)=v₅(c₂)=4, residues c₁/625=c₂/625=3 mod 5, and v₅(c_j)≥6 for 3≤j≤39. Hence P is in Z₅[X] with reduction 3X(X+1); the derivative residues at 0 and 4 are 3 and 2. Hensel gives exactly one root in each of those discs, and none in the three other discs. On a root disc the difference quotient at the root is a unit, so the full integer valuation law follows, not merely a pattern at finitely many moduli. For i≥0 the count is positive by placing 39 single-box cores in distinct components. The two disjoint root classes give density 2/5^t for excess valuation at least t≥1; successive subtraction gives 3/5 at valuation 4 and 8/5^(e+1) at 4+e. This establishes only the one coefficient at n=39, not sufficiency for lifting the whole progression.
